text:
sanjay: Thinking about a cleaner split between the intake/ingest path and the bench/prober orchestration. current flow is too coupled, makes fast-path admits slow. thoughts?
tess: +1. we've hit this with quantized binaries — bench spikes stall ingestion.
alex: can you sketch the boundary you want? interface surface?
sanjay: idea: small RPC boundary — ingest hands off a ModelDescriptor and a light health-check cookie, bench service claims and runs probes independently. ingest only waits for a small readiness verdict for fast-path. deep bench runs async.
chao: so basic contract: READY/DEFER/REJECT and an async evaluation id for later metrics?
sanjay: exactly. READY = ok to serve with fallback telemetry; DEFER = needs manual or longer bench; REJECT = block. async eval id used to attach golden-samples and regressions.
tess: how do we prevent a thundering herd when many models are in DEFER? also cost concerns.
alex: admission policy should have rate-limits and a quota for heavy benches per org. plus sampling priority.
chao: also need clear shape for the ModelDescriptor: backbone, weights hash, tokenizer id, seq_len_hint, quantization profile id. minimal to avoid churn.
sanjay: here's a tiny proto we sketched:
```
service OnboardProber {
  rpc Probe(ModelDescriptor) returns (ProbeDecision);
  rpc ProbeStatus(ProbeTicket) returns (ProbeResult);
}
message ModelDescriptor {
  string model_id = 1;
  string weights_hash = 2;
  string tokenizer = 3;
  int32 seq_len_hint = 4;
  string quant_profile = 5;
}
message ProbeDecision {
  enum Decision { READY = 0; DEFER = 1; REJECT = 2; }
  Decision decision = 1;
  string ticket = 2; // optional for async
}
```
chao: proto looks good. add a small hints map for bench config (golden_sample_bucket, latency_sla).
tess: agree. also need a backchannel so bench can request a cache-warmup workspace from runtime infra (prefetch weights, compile artifacts).
infra-bot: deploy queued: bench-worker-v2 at 1765559980 -> 1765560005 :rocket:
sanjay: thanks infra-bot. on the policy side we should define: fast-path acceptance bar = smoke perf + tokenization parity + kv-cache sanity. any objections?
natalie: tokenization parity is critical for correctness. we should fail fast on tokenizer mismatch. maybe a pre-tokenizer step in ingest.
alex: tradeoffs: stricter fast-path = fewer false positives but longer time to serve; looser fast-path = more rollbacks and customer impact. need telemetry to decide the sweet spot.
tess: propose feature-flagged rollout. start with strict bar for a week, collect false positive/rejection signals, then relax.
sanjay: agreed. also add a cost-metering tag to probe tickets so Finance can bucket bench spend per model/team.
chao: for long-term: consider a probe-runner pool decoupled from clusters that serve traffic. probe-runner can emulate different runtimes (onnx, triton, native) and return normalized metrics.
natalie: plus a canonical golden set for semantic regressions. keep small but representative. maintain per-model failure artifacts.
alex: one more interface concern: how do we version the decision schema? ProbeDecision might need v2 with more structured failure reasons. add a schema_version header.
sanjay: good call. add schema_version + nonblocking list of failure_codes.
tess: operational question — how do we surface partial readiness? e.g., READY but missing kv-cache warmed; runtime should serve with degraded latency or fallback.
chao: include readiness_flags in ProbeDecision: {kv_warm: bool, compiled: bool, quant_ok: bool}. runtime uses flags to route to fallback models or warm-up buckets.
sanjay: ok next steps: 1) alex to draft proto w/ hints map and readiness_flags; 2) tess to write rollout/feature flag plan + quotas; 3) chao to prototype probe-runner shim; 4) natalie to define golden-sample set criteria. i'll prep a short RFC follow-up with tradeoffs.
alex: will start proto today, ping me for review.
tess: i'll draft rollout doc and spike telemetry dashboards.
chao: I'll hack on runner shim this afternoon.
natalie: will assemble initial golden set and tests.
sanjay: cool. if folks can have first drafts by EOD Thurs we can sync Fri. :thumbsup:
tess: ack.
alex: ack.
chao: ack.
